title: The Taste of the Same Donkey
summary: A traveling quack physician arrived in the village selling "Miraculous Elixir of Arabian Gazelle," claiming a single drop cured all ailments. He charged ten silver pieces per vial....
keywords: the taste of the same donkey
full_text:
A traveling quack physician arrived in the village selling "Miraculous Elixir of Arabian Gazelle," claiming a single drop cured all ailments. He charged ten silver pieces per vial.

Nasruddin, suspecting a fraud, bought a vial, tasted a drop, and immediately spit it out: "Why, this is nothing but plain ditch water mixed with donkey vinegar!"

The quack became indignant: "How dare an ignorant villager insult imperial medicine! Bring me ten sick men, and I will prove its celestial potency!"

Nasruddin returned with his own wooden jug filled with water from his garden cistern. He had two villagers taste both the quack's potion and his own cistern water. Both villagers agreed that Nasruddin's water tasted much sweeter and fresher.

"You see?" announced Nasruddin to the crowd. "The quack sells sour donkey vinegar in gold vials, while my donkey gives pure spring water for free! Keep your silver coins in your pockets, and drink fresh water from your own wells!"
moral: Blind faith in labels often deceives people into accepting ordinary reality as magic.
